slides.title: Rules that predict
slides.text: A model is a rule that predicts what will happen, like: distance = 2 × height. A simulation runs the rule so you can check it.
slides.say: A model is a rule that predicts what will happen, like: distance is 2 times the height. A simulation runs the rule so you can check it.
slides.alt: The Ramp Rule case: a rule that predicts how far a car rolls, with the ramp and the trials waiting.

slides.title: Predict, compare, refine
slides.text: Predict with the model. Run real trials. Compare. If they disagree, change the model, not the data, and test again.
slides.alt: The model has run: predicted distances sit beside the real trials, so the rule can be compared and refined.

slides.title: The ramp
slides.text: Every trial went farther than predicted, so the rule is too low. Refine it, and the error gets smaller.
slides.alt: The ramp trials ran farther than the first rule predicted, so the rule was raised and run again: the error shrinks.

slides.title: One trial is not proof
slides.text: One lucky trial proves nothing. Compare the model with many results. To balance a game, test 20 runs, not one.
slides.alt: Bounce Back: another model case with its own trials, because one lucky trial never proves a rule.
